summary: Even a worker who finds a good employer after a layoff is usually paid a lower hourly wage for years.
realLife: A Washington State study of Great Recession layoffs found losses came mainly from lower wage rates that recovered slowly, and lost ties between worker and employer explained over half of them.
sources: NBER working paper w24217, Sources of Displaced Workers' Long-Term Earnings Losses: https://www.nber.org/papers/w24217
inGame: pay on the person's job records before and after; years at old employer set the size of the match lost.

turns.summary: A well-matched worker's pay climbs back at the new job within a year.
The worker's pay stays below the old level for years.
pulledBy: long tenure at the old employer
skills specific to the old firm
turns.writesBack: job records show lower pay; journal note

turns.summary: The worker blames the old employer and tells neighbors.
turns.writesBack: neighbor tie closer; tie to ex-boss colder
